Traffic Commission Meeting
Public Comment from the Audience
•
If you wish to address the Traffic Commission, please complete a Speaker Request Card, as it must be handed to the City Clerk before the start of the meeting.
•
The Traffic Commission will hear public comments on matters not listed on the agenda during the Public Comments from the Audience period.
•
Opportunity to address the Traffic Commission (on non-agenda items) is limited to 3 minutes per speaker.
•
The Traffic Commission will hear public comments on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote.
Brown Act
Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.
Rules of Decorum
Persons attending the meeting shall observe rules of propriety, decorum, good conduct, and refrain from impertinent or slanderous remarks. Violation of this rule shall result in such persons being barred from further audience before the governing body. Pursuant to Gov. Code Sect. 54954.3(c), any person who engages in unlawful interference shall be removed from chambers.
Americans with Disabilities Act
In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, please contact the City Clerk's office at least 48 hours prior to the meeting to allow the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to the meeting or service.
This agenda was posted 72 hours in advance of the meeting at the City Hall, 8838 E. Valley Boulevard, Rosemead; the L.A. County Library, Rosemead Branch, 8800 E. Valley Boulevard, Rosemead; and other locations pursuant to RMC Sec. 1.08.020. Any writings or documents provided to a majority of the Rosemead Traffic Commission regarding any item on this agenda will be made available for public inspection in the City Clerk's office during normal business hours.

A.
Traffic Calming Measures for Various Street Segments (6 Segments)
SUMMARY
The City of Rosemead received a request to evaluate various street segments for the installation of speed humps, and other traffic calming measures. In response to this request and on behalf of the City, engineering staff has completed a traffic review of each segment to determine if the street segments qualify for the installation of traffic calming measures.
LOCATION 1: PINE STREET BETWEEN GARVEY AVENUE AND GRAVES AVENUE
The City of Rosemead has received a request to review the segment of Pine Street, between Garvey Avenue and Graves Avenue. The city is requesting to evaluate this segment for the installation of speed humps, and other traffic calming measures. In response to this request and on behalf of the City, engineering staff has completed a traffic review of this segment of Pine Street to determine if the street segment qualifies for the installation of traffic calming measures.
After a thorough review of existing field and traffic conditions and per the guidelines in the California Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (CAMUTCD), California Vehicle Code (CVC), and based on engineering judgement, it was determined that the segment along Pine Street between Garvey Avenue and Graves Avenue meets the requirements for the installation of traffic calming devices along the street.
1.
REMOVE AND REPLACE SPEED LIMIT SIGN (R2 - 1): Remove the existing "20" Speed Limit sign that is located along the west side of Pine Avenue, approximately 960-ft north of Graves Avenue. Replace sign with a "25" Speed Limit Sign (R2-1).
a.
The adopted Citywide Speed Survey for the City of Rosemead has a speed of 25 MPH along this segment. If the "20 MPH" sign is left posted along Pine Street, then it is not enforceable by the police department when using radar.
2.
REMOVE AND REPLACE SPEED LIMIT SIGN (R2 - 1): Remove the existing "20" Speed Limit sign that is located along the east side of Pine Avenue, approximately 630-ft north of Graves Avenue. Replace sign with a "25" Speed Limit Sign (R2-1).
a.
The adopted Citywide Speed Survey for the City of Rosemead has a speed of 25 MPH along this segment. If the "20 MPH" sign is left posted along Pine Street, then it is not enforceable by the police department when using radar.
3.
INSTALL NEW SPEED LIMIT SIGN (R2 - 1): Install new "25" Speed Limit sign along the west side of Pine Avenue, approximately 160-ft south of Garvey Avenue (R2-1).
4.
INSTALL SPEED FEEDBACK SIGN: Install Speed Feedback Sign at the following locations:
a.
Install one speed feedback sign under the proposed "25" speed limit sign, located along the west side of Pine Avenue, approximately 960-ft north of Graves Avenue.
b.
Install one speed feedback sign under the proposed "25" speed limit sign, located along the east side of Pine Avenue, approximately 630-ft north of Graves Avenue.
5.
INSTALL "25" PAVEMENT LEGENDS ADJACENT TO SIGNAGE: Install "25" Pavement Legends adjacent to the new 25 MPH Speed Limit Signage along Pine Street, between Garvey Avenue and Graves Avenue.
6.
INSTALL DOUBLE YELLOW CENTERLINE: Install double yellow centerline along Pine Street, from Garvey Avenue to Newmark Avenue, and along Pine Street from Newmark Avenue to Graves Avenue. Install the double yellow centerline along the entire segment of Pine Street.
Staff Report
